findings.passage: We need common sense election security measures such as voter ID to ensure the integrity at the ballot box. The people of North Carolina passed voter ID... in 2018, only to be overruled by activist judges.
findings.note: Candidate profile for the 2024 NC House 9 primary, in the Voting and Elections section, quoting his statement. Exact day not shown on the page.

findings.motion: Second Reading, HB 958 Election Law Changes (66-47)
findings.note: Reeder is listed among the ayes. The bill narrows who may hand-deliver an absentee ballot, requires a statement of US citizenship on voter registration, and requires military-overseas voters to send a copy of photo ID.

findings.motion: M11 Concur, HB 958 Election Law Changes (62-47)
findings.note: Reeder is listed among the ayes on the House vote to concur with the Senate changes. The bill page shows the governor vetoed it on 2026-08-17.

findings.motion: UNC School of Government summary of HB 958 House committee substitute, as context for the two votes above
findings.note: Summary text: "Now requires, in GS 163-258.10, covered voters to submit the military-overseas ballot with the copy of the identification described in GS 163-166.16(a)(photo identification required to vote in person) instead of the six categories of identification originally listed in the act." Also: county boards "can also only process a voter registration application if the voter affirmatively indicates that they are a US citizen." This is a bill summary, not Reeder's words.
NC House, Third Reading (roll call #810), 2024-12-11: yea (tally 73–45); census gate: none.
subjects: photo ID for all voters (constitutional amendment, in person and by mail)
